With a price of ₹2000+ for two, it offers good value for the quality provided. One visit is sure to make you come back for more!

Food:
Having explored various Chinese dishes before, we decided to rely on the server’s recommendations, and they did not disappoint! The food was served piping hot, bursting with flavors. Do note that some items may be discontinued or unavailable at times, depending on the menu updates.

Soups: The Veg Eight Treasure Soup was a great way to kickstart the meal, setting the perfect tone.

Starters: The Crispy Corn Chilly Pepper had a unique crunch and was full of flavor.

Main Course: The Veg Lemon Grass Fried Rice carried a subtle yet delightful lemongrass aroma. The Veg Nasi Goreng had a well-balanced taste, and the Stir-Fried Chicken with Chilly Garlic & Hot Basil was delicious, though the texture was slightly inconsistent.

Curries & Noodles: The Chicken Thai Red Curry had a rich taste, but the boiled chicken didn’t do it justice—battered pieces would be a better alternative. The Lotus Stem & Asparagus in Red Curry Infusion is a must-try if you enjoy bold flavors. The Wok Tossed Noodles were fairly standard Hakka noodles. The interiors feature Chinese script carvings, adding an authentic touch, while the background music enhances the experience. The space is decent but not extraordinary.

The lounge is located inside Palm Beach Galleria Mall, Sector 19D, Vashi, Navi Mumbai – on the rooftop, just like other popular spots in the building.

The total bill came to ₹6688 (including taxes). Here’s what we ordered:

2 Butter Rotis – ₹109 each
1 Butter Chicken – ₹669
5 Butter Naans – ₹99 each
1 Cheesy Fries – ₹384
3 Fresh Lime Sodas – ₹210 each
1 Hakka Noodles – ₹428
1 Murg Tikka Masala – ₹637
1 Non-Veg Platter – ₹1499
3 Virgin Mojitos – ₹440 each
1 Water Bottle – ₹90

The ambience was nice, and although they had live music, it hadn’t started by the time we were there, so we missed out on that part of the experience. Still, the setting was good for a small group celebration.

The food quality was very nice, and everyone at the table enjoyed what was served. Service was decent, and the overall vibe of the place felt modern and chill.

However, the one major disappointment was the pricing of the water bottle — ₹90 for a Bisleri bottle with MRP of ₹20 felt extremely unnecessary and overpriced. For larger groups, these small add-ons can become an unpleasant surprise on the final bill. That part definitely felt like a setback.

The place is otherwise well-suited for small group dinners, celebrations, and casual evenings. The seating is spacious, and the rooftop layout adds to the experience.

Overall, I’d say it was a good time with friends — food and setting were on point, but small things like inflated water prices take away from the experience.

- Sprite : It’s Sprite. Did its job.

Loved this place and the vibe., name_person=Jayesh Tiwari}", "{guided_block={GUIDED_DINING_MEAL_TYPE=Dinner, GUIDED_DINING_PRICE_RANGE=₹1,400–1,600, GUIDED_DINING_FOOD_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_SERVICE_ASPECT=5, GUIDED_DINING_MODE=Dine in, GUIDED_DINING_ATMOSPHERE_ASPECT=5}, time_line=7 months ago, review=What’s Your Plan is located in Sakinaka and it is behind the famous McDonalds and you have ample parking space available.

It might sound cliché, but this is the first time I’m genuinely using the term hidden gem — this place truly surprised me with how good it was in every aspect.

The restaurant is spacious with two different sections being available. One is AC with high chair seatings and a bar plus DJ space too and the other is Non AC causal seatings with pool table in the center and a nice bar. Loved the use of the space and the wall designs as it looked really happening. Currently as IPL is going on they have decorated the Non AC section with team flags and have kept a big screen too.

The menu here is vast and they have options available in Indian, Asian, Italian and some more cuisines. Right now they have added a limited edition mango menu too. Apart from this they have various offers in food and drinks specially for big groups for IPL season. Prices are at par with similar type of brands and the quantity served is good.

Went here on a Monday dinner and the kitchen service was on time and table service by staff Mantu was great as he was polite and knew the menu well.

What We Had -
APPETISERS~
Jamaican Jerk Spice Chicken Tikka -
Served in a unique way as hanging skewers in the Dubai frame. Served with buttery naan, onion and green chutney this was juicy chicken tikkas done in green Jamaican spices. Loved the taste of this as it was not the regular tikka and the spices had nice hint of hotness to it.

Genkai Prawns Maki Roll -
Surprisingly a very nice and tasty sushi served. Fresh prawns rolled nicely with rice and the crunchy tempura coating with spicy sauce tasted excellent. Loved everything about this sushi as it was bang on tasty.

MAINS~
Mushroom & Truffle Cream Cheese Flatbread -
Thin base topped with generous amount of cheese, mushrooms, red chillies, cream cheese and sprayed with aromatic and earthy truffle oil looked perfect and tasted delicious. Loved the juicy mushrooms and the cream cheese and they were honest in using the truffle oil hence a perfect dish again.

Nasi Goreng -
This was a complete miss for me as it was way different from the Nasi Goreng that I have been eating for years. Maybe it is their way as I felt it was a plain normal fried rice however being fried rice it tasted nice but for Nasi Goreng they need to check the recipe.

DESSERT~
Mango Cheesecake -
Again a very different version of cheesecake as this was more closer to a baked layered malai cake with mango flavour and topped with Alphonse mango. Taste wise it was really good as the mango was sweet and it was not extra sweet.

MOCKTAILS~
Tropical Bliss.
Sunset Bloom.
Both the mocktails tasted refreshing as the ingredients tasted nice with each other.

So our meal at What’s Your Plan was really good as the food tasted perfect, the ambiance plus vibe of the restaurant is great and the service was excellent. [{'name_person': 'sam mahtani', 'time_line': 'a month ago', 'review': 'Mumbai, and especially Bandra West (with another outlet in Churchgate), should be delighted to welcome Mezcalita—a bright and comfortable Mexican cantina/taquería. The service, led by Pinku and his team, is caring, attentive, and genuinely warm, while the food strikes a perfect balance between creativity and authenticity.

The menu is vibrant and visually engaging, guiding guests toward a true Mexican culinary adventure, with comfort food taking center stage.

The Guacamole (GUAC), made with fresh Hass avocados, delivers a creamy texture and rich, buttery flavor. Blended with tomatoes, onions, a dash of lime, and a subtle kick of habanero chilies, it is simply delicious and divine.

I  was especially blown away by the habanero-laced cottage cheese cubes, paired with soy protein and other fresh ingredients. This appetizer is packed with flavor and offers great value for money. Pro tip: always pair it with a glass of Horchata—Mexico’s national drink—made from rice milk, cardamom, cinnamon, and both evaporated and condensed milk.

Mezcalita also shows its sensibility by baking its own bread for the Tortas (Mexican sandwiches). The Telera buns, with their crisp crust and fluffy interior, elevate the experience. The cottage cheese Chilaquiles Torta was an absolute delight.

The black bean vegetarian burritos were impressively well-balanced and just the right size for a single taster portion.

For your next Mexican culinary journey, head to Mezcalita at Pali Hill. Explore their wide range of cocktails, and don’t hesitate to reach out to Pinku, the manager, for a thoughtfully chosen table.

Final note: Mezcalita isn’t just a restaurant—it’s a celebration of Mexican flavors brought to life with care, creativity, and authenticity.
